agencies.src/lib/auth/create-user-record.ts: The agency is created with the account. Provisioning is idempotent and lives only here — the signup route and the auth callback both delegate, after a period where both provisioned and raced.
agencies.src/app/api/settings/account/route.ts: The agency name and timezone as edited in settings.

analytics_reports.src/features/analytics/actions/report-ac: Saved-report CRUD behind the analytics screen.
analytics_reports.src/features/analytics/lib/purge-account: Deletes a client's reports as part of the Meta data-deletion cascade. Not a second way to delete one report — it takes no report id.

brand_kit_extractions.src/lib/visual/queries.ts: The only store for a brand-extraction run.

brand_profiles.src/features/clients/actions/client-acti: createClient seeds the profile; updateBrandProfile is the client screen's editor.
brand_profiles.src/features/analytics/lib/online-follow: refreshObservedBestTime — the only writer of best_time_json and best_time_updated_at, and it only ever writes measured Instagram data. The guessed path was deleted 2026-08-31.
brand_profiles.src/app/(dashboard)/clients/[id]/sources: A lazy backfill of pillar ids on first open, for clients that predate them. Writes content_pillars only. The comment beside it records why the web-research row is deliberately NOT created here: a page render must not decide whether the pipeline searches the web.
brand_profiles.src/features/clients/lib/provision-clien: provisionClient — the ONE way a client and its mandatory children are created. The onboarding form and solo signup both build them here; before 2026-08-31 solo signup built them by hand and shipped without a visual identity, without a web-research row, and without a rollback.

brand_visual_identity.src/lib/visual/queries.ts: The only store for a client's visual identity — a whole-row upsert at extraction and a blob patch for edits.

client_ideas.src/features/ideas/lib/ideas.ts: The whole client-ideas lifecycle (submit, status, link to post, mark read) in one file.

client_sources.src/features/sources/actions/source-acti: The source manager's CRUD. createSource and updateSource both resolve the URL through resolveSourceUrl — they did not, and updateSource was a live SSRF hole until 2026-08-31.
reportStatus stamps last_fetched_at / last_fetch_status / last_fetch_error after a fetch. Fetch health, written by the fetcher; it never touches a source's configuration.
client_sources.src/lib/clients/sync-source-pillars.ts: removeDeletedPillarIds writes ONE column, pillar_ids, as a cascade of a pillar deletion — reachable only through updateBrandProfile, never from the sources screen. updateSource writes the same column when the user scopes a source, which is a different operation. (An earlier note here said 'config' and called this open audit business; both were wrong.)
client_sources.src/features/clients/lib/provision-clien: provisionClient — the ONE way a client and its mandatory children are created. The onboarding form and solo signup both build them here; before 2026-08-31 solo signup built them by hand and shipped without a visual identity, without a web-research row, and without a rollback.

client_style_memos.src/ai/learning/distill-style-memo.ts: The memo's only writer, next to the distiller that produces it.

clients.src/features/clients/actions/client-acti: create, update and delete from the clients screen.
clients.src/features/clients/lib/provision-clien: provisionClient — the ONE way a client and its mandatory children are created. The onboarding form and solo signup both build them here; before 2026-08-31 solo signup built them by hand and shipped without a visual identity, without a web-research row, and without a rollback.

discarded_drafts.src/lib/queries/discarded-drafts.ts: One insert for both discard sources (wizard, review). reason stays optional — distill-style-memo filters on it being non-null.

generation_runs.src/lib/generation/runs.ts: start and finish, paired in one file so a run cannot be opened without a way to close it.

generation_themes.src/lib/generation/runs.ts: Themes belong to a run and are tracked beside it.

idea_form_tokens.src/features/ideas/lib/ideas.ts: getOrCreateToken — the idea form's link, minted beside the ideas it collects.

ig_account_metrics.src/features/analytics/lib/account-metri: upsertAccountMetricDays — the only writer. There were six inline upserts across sync-metrics, refresh-window and online-followers, each restating the onConflict target. Callers write PARTIAL rows on purpose (reach in one pass, day totals in another, online-follower hours in a third) so no pass nulls a column another owns; that is why this is a thin shared upsert and not a whole-row writer.
ig_account_metrics.src/features/analytics/lib/purge-account: [hand-listed] purgeAccountAnalytics deletes this table through a `scoped(table)` helper, so `.from(table)` never names it and the scan cannot find it. Meta's data-deletion callback and an account switch; deleteClient deliberately leans on the `clients` cascade instead.

syncDemographicsWeekly, beside the sync that fetches it.
ig_audience_snapshots.src/features/analytics/lib/purge-account: [hand-listed] purgeAccountAnalytics deletes this table through a `scoped(table)` helper, so `.from(table)` never names it and the scan cannot find it. Meta's data-deletion callback and an account switch; deleteClient deliberately leans on the `clients` cascade instead.

syncClientComments — the half-hourly capture, and the only writer that brings comments IN. Upserts on Instagram's own comment id and deletes rows the API stopped returning for a post it just refetched, which is how an upstream delete reaches us.
ig_comments.src/features/comments/actions/comment-ac: The three moderation actions, each recording the change it just made on Instagram: a reply inserts its own row so the comment reads as answered now rather than after the next cron, hide flips the flag, delete removes the comment and its replies. Not a second sync — the same fact the cron would have brought back, written early by the party that caused it.
ig_comments.src/features/analytics/lib/purge-account: [hand-listed] purgeAccountAnalytics deletes this table through a `scoped(table)` helper, so `.from(table)` never names it and the scan cannot find it. This table is the one it touches that holds data about people who are neither the agency nor its client, which makes this line the part of Meta's data-deletion callback that erases third parties.

ig_post_metrics.src/features/analytics/lib/post-metrics-: upsertPostMetricRows — the only writer, for the same reason account-metrics-store is: two jobs now write this table and nothing else would keep their conflict target in step. Callers write PARTIAL rows on purpose — the nightly sync writes identity AND measurements, the half-hourly comments sync writes identity only (caption, permalink, thumbnail, post_id) because the queue renders the post a comment sits under and cannot wait until 03:30 for it. The comments sync must never write the measurement columns: a zero there is indistinguishable from a measured zero on the analytics page.
ig_post_metrics.src/features/analytics/lib/purge-account: [hand-listed] purgeAccountAnalytics deletes this table through a `scoped(table)` helper, so `.from(table)` never names it and the scan cannot find it. Meta's data-deletion callback and an account switch; deleteClient deliberately leans on the `clients` cascade instead.

intelligence_briefings.src/features/dashboard/lib/write-briefin: writeWeeklyBriefing — the only composer of a briefing.
intelligence_briefings.src/app/api/cron/generate/route.ts: Patches coaching_points onto a briefing writeWeeklyBriefing has just returned, for solo agencies only. A second call into the briefing writer would need it to accept a field it cannot compute; this stays a patch by id.

notifications.src/components/layout/shell-context.tsx: The browser toggling is_read for the signed-in user, optimistically. Read state only — it can never create a notification, and it is RLS-scoped rather than admin.
notifications.src/lib/notifications/notify.ts: notify() — the only insert. There were five, four bypassing the dedup. Cooldown is a per-caller decision (NOTIFY_EVERY_TIME), not blanket: two approval emails in a week are two events.

post_approval_tokens.src/features/approval-portal/lib/approva: createApprovalBatch mints the week's tokens, clearing any superseded batch first.
post_approval_tokens.src/features/approval-portal/actions/app: submitApproval records the client's decision on the token they arrived with.
post_approval_tokens.src/lib/actions/post-actions.ts: resolveChangeRequest closes a change request from the agency side.

post_canvas_docs.src/lib/canvas/doc-store.ts: upsertCanvasDoc for an edit, insertCanvasDocs when a post is created with docs already made.

post_history.src/lib/queries/post-history.ts: recordPostTopics — the cron batch and the approve route both record topics, and were writing the identical row from two files until 2026-08-31.

post_images.src/features/assets/lib/storage.ts: putPostImage / putPostImages — the only way an image lands at a position. There were four, three of which deleted the row and its file before inserting, so a failed insert lost the picture.
post_images.src/app/api/posts/[id]/images/route.ts: DELETE removes a slide the user deleted. A removal, not a write of an image — it has no row to put.

posting_schedules.src/features/clients/actions/client-acti: createClient seeds it; updateSchedule is the schedule editor.
posting_schedules.src/features/clients/lib/provision-clien: provisionClient — the ONE way a client and its mandatory children are created. The onboarding form and solo signup both build them here; before 2026-08-31 solo signup built them by hand and shipped without a visual identity, without a web-research row, and without a rollback.

posts.src/lib/actions/post-actions.ts: The agency's edits: updatePost (nine validated columns), savePostCopy (caption and slides, partial — the calendar saves a caption with no slides), persistRewrite, schedulePosts, deletePost.
posts.src/app/api/posts/route.ts: POST creates a post from an approved wizard draft, through draftColumns.
posts.src/app/api/cron/generate/route.ts: The nightly batch inserts generated drafts, through the same draftColumns.
posts.src/features/publishing/lib/publish-post: claimPost takes a post for publishing and markPublished/markFailed record the outcome. Three operations in one file BY DESIGN — they are the states of one lifecycle, and the registry cannot see a fourth added here.
posts.src/app/api/posts/[id]/publish/route.ts: Publish-now sets the post publishing before handing off, so the manual path takes the same claim the cron does.
posts.src/features/calendar/actions/post-recov: rearmFailedPost — the user putting a failed post back in the queue. The only place attempts are reset.
posts.src/app/api/cron/visuals/route.ts: The visuals lane's own attempt counter and status, which is separate from the publish counter on purpose.
posts.src/lib/visual/post-color.ts: claimScheme — a compare-and-swap on visual_ground/visual_accent so two lanes generating one carousel cannot split its colours.

social_connections.src/app/api/meta/callback/route.ts: connectInstagram stores the connection the OAuth flow just produced.
social_connections.src/features/publishing/lib/refresh-toke: Two of the five Meta-side credential operations: rotate an expiring token without the user, and retire one Meta has declared dead (access_token = null) so publish reports 'needs reconnecting' instead of hammering Graph. Both update by id and neither touches account identity.
recordSyncHealth stamps last_sync_at / last_sync_error, and is their only writer. It never touches a token. It updates by (client_id, platform), which is exactly one row: social_connections_client_id_platform_key makes that pair UNIQUE — the same index the meta callback's onConflict relies on.
social_connections.src/app/api/meta/data-deletion/route.ts: Meta's data-deletion callback erases the connection. Required by the platform and deliberately unconditional.
social_connections.src/app/api/canva/callback/route.ts: Stores the Canva connection from its OAuth flow.
social_connections.src/app/api/canva/canva-auth.ts: Refreshes the Canva token. Separate provider, separate lifetime, separate refresh endpoint.
social_connections.src/features/settings/actions/canva-acti: The user disconnecting Canva. Uses the service-role client BY NECESSITY: the only policy on this table is keyed on client_id, and a Canva row is owned by a user so its client_id is NULL — a user-scoped delete would match nothing and report success. Ownership is proven in TypeScript instead; see the comment at the call site.
social_connections.src/features/settings/actions/team-actio: removeTeamMember takes the departing member's personal integrations with them. Distinct from disconnectCanvaConnection (that is the owner choosing to unlink); this is the workspace removing someone. Added 2026-08-31 because social_connections.user_id is NO ACTION, so removing a member who held a Canva connection raised 23503 and surfaced as a message the admin could not act on.

users.src/lib/auth/create-user-record.ts: The user row is created with the account, with the email guard — that column is a lookup key and a blank one is an account nobody can recover.
